analytic.title: EDF Scheduling for Tasks with Uncertain Execution Times in Networked Control System

div.p: The execution times of the real-time tasks are uncertain in the networked control system. So the classical scheduling algorithms are not suitable for deciding the priorities of tasks. On the basis of the classical EDF, this paper proposes the static extension EDF scheduling algorithm according to the uncertainty of the execution times. This algorithm can get the distribution function of the schedulability variable according to the distribution functions of tasks with the fuzzy theory. Then the value of schedulability variable which is satisfied the scheduling of the system can be determined by the possibility and necessity of the schedulability variable. The suitable execution time of each task can be calculated to decide the priority of each task. So the order of data can be decided. This algorithm is very simple and overcomes the disadvantage of not deciding priority by fuzzy time in classical scheduling algorithm. Also, it keeps the advantage of high occupancy rate of the resources. It is proved that this algorithm can schedule well under uncertainty.

div.head: 1． Introduction
div.p: Networked control system (NCS) is a closed-loop feedback control system through a real time communication network. Messages are transmit between distributed objects through public or private computer network. However, due to the characteristics of network sharing resources, the scheduling is inevitable. With the system more and more complex and the expansion of distribution space, the real-time and control performance are seriously affected. Therefore, it is not enough to analyze and design the NCS only from the perspective of control. So, in order to improve the running performance of network, it is necessary to introduce reasonable scheduling strategies while studying the resource scheduling [1] .

The scheduling on network is divided into two categories, one is the non-preemptive scheduling of data sharing the same transmission medium, the other is the preemptive scheduling of tasks sharing the CPU resource. Wei Zhang extended the CPU scheduling to network scheduling [2] [3] . Because scheduling on network is similar to task scheduling in CPU, that is, they both have limited resources. Tasks can't use CPU resource at the same time in CPU scheduling. While data are transmit in the same medium. There should be one data package in the medium at the same time with time-sharing transmission. The difference lies in the non-preemption of network scheduling. That is, the data package can't be interrupt once it is transmit on the network.

Wang Huayong, ect. used the mode of MVSM (Markov vector space model) to deal with the uncertainty of the tasks [4] . It predicts the execution time to reduce the influence of the uncertain execution time.

This paper studies the scheduling algorithm in CPU to improve the situation of data transmission on the network. The problem of uncertainty in process of execution is dealt with preemptive EDF scheduling algorithm on the basis of fuzzy theory. Based on the scope of execution time, a precise execution time can be got with the extension EDF fuzzy scheduling algorithm. It can get satisfactory scheduling effect using the precise time to execute the scheduling. The algorithm is simple and also retains the advantage of high resource utilization in EDF scheduling.

div.head: Classical EDF scheduling algorithm
div.p: The earliest deadline first scheduling algorithm is a dynamic optimal scheduling . It is also a preemptive scheduling. The tasks scheduled by this algorithm should satisfy the following constraints: each real-time task must be finished before the deadline and have a constant running time [5] .

The priority is determined by the distance between the current moment and the deadline in EDF [6] . The shorter the distance is the higher the priority is. The algorithm adjusts the priorities only when the tasks are ready to be scheduled. At other moments, the tasks keep the same order, that is to say, the priorities of the tasks are unchanged. So, EDF always choose the most urgent task to obtain the processor. Its scheduling process is, in a new ready state, the scheduler chooses the task with the earliest deadline from the ready tasks and provides all resource to the task. The earliest deadline will be recalculated at the arrival of the mew tasks to result a new state. If the new task's priority is higher than that of the running task, the scheduler will stop the running task to execute the new task. When the new task is finished, the scheduler will continue to execute the interrupted task according EDF algorithm.

For classical algorithm, execution time is defined on the assumption that the tasks are fully independent and there is no unforeseen communication delay. In fact, all tasks will compete for the same CPU resource. The execution time of each task depends on the operation of CPU. And the more the tasks, the longer the execution time. So, the execution time is a fuzzy scope instead of a fixed value.

div.head: EDF scheduling with uncertain execution time
div.p: Fuzzy theory is a mathematical tool to solve the problem of uncertainty. It has been successfully applied in control theory, decision-making, optimization and other fields. The outstanding merit of fuzzy theory is similar to human thinking. It can summarize and reflect human experience. It is also very convenient to deal quantitatively with the qualitative rules. In order to deal with the fuzzy execution time, it is necessary to modify EDF algorithm from two aspects: the schedulability criteria and the algorithm itself.

div.head: The scheduling strategies
div.p: The first aim of scheduling strategies is to provide possible schedules, and the second one is to choose the best scheduling method. To a given set of tasks, this can guarantee more tasks to be executed with higher possibility.

For a fuzzy time scope, there are two special times corresponding to a function value: the maximal time and the minimal time. There are two scheduling strategies: pessimistic and optimistic scheduling, using maximal time and the minimal time respectively [8] . In this case, it is not needed to redefine the scheduling algorithm. It uses the maximal and minimal time to replace the precise time. In order to get better scheduling, this paper adjusts the EDF algorithm: to calculate execution time of each task by the Necessity and Possibility values of the schedulability variable G.

The schedulability variable G relates to ∏(G≤1) and N(G≤1). Following three conditions correspond to specific scheduling strategy: case A: If the value of π G (g) is maximum, G>1.Then, 0<∏(G≤1)=α<1，N(G≤1)=0. The optimistic scheduling is applied. The execution time is considered to be close to the minimal. It guarantees the possibility of schedulability equal to α to apply the minimal time. The execution time of each task is minimum on the condition that the value of π ei (t) equal to α. If ∏(G≤1)=0, it means that the set of tasks can't be scheduled. case B: If the value of π G (g) is maximum, G<1. Then ∏(G≤1)=1, 0<N(G≤1)=1-β≤1. The pessimistic scheduling is applied. The execution time of each task is considered to be close to maximum. The maximal execution time can guarantee the necessity of schedulability equal to 1-β. The execution time of each task is maximum on the condition that the value of π ei (t) equal to β. If N(G≤1)=1, it means that the set of tasks can be scheduled in any case. EDF algorithm can guarantee all tasks applying the maximal execution time to be finished before the deadline.
case C: If the value of π G (g) is maximal, G=1. Then ∏(G≤1)=1，N(G≤1)=0. The execution time of each task can be got on the condition that π ei (t)= 1.

div.head: Result and analysis
div.p: In order to verify the feasibility of the scheduling, this paper studies the networked control system. The networked control system is shown in figure 2. A controller controls three motor through the network. The input is step signal. Sensors are time-driven, while actuators and controller are event-driven. Each sensor samples data periodically. But each of them has to share the same transmission path, it has to consider scheduling the data of each sensor. The scheduler is a computer, which can change the analog signals sampled by sensors into digital signals that can be dealt with computer. It also can schedule the tasks generated by sensors with the EDF fuzzy scheduling algorithm and decide the order of the task in application layer to send the data to network orderly.

At this time, ∏(G≤1)=0.8182 ， N(G≤1)=0. So the optimistic scheduling is accepted. The execution times are the minimum corresponding to ∏(G≤1)=0.8182. e 1 =0.0048, e 2 = 0.0058, e 3 =0.0068.

Figure 6 and Figure 7 are the scheduling of the network and output of the system on the assumption that execution times are precise. The top graph shows the scheduling of the scheduler's data on the network, while the below one shows the scheduling of the controller's data on the network in Figure 2and Figure 6.

Comparing Figures 2 and6, Figures 3 and7, the scheduling is out of order at time 4s when the execution time is uncertain. In this case, the data can't be transmitted in a long time, which can cause system instable. When the precise time calculated by the fuzzy theory is accepted, the scheduling is well and the system is stable. Case 2: T 1 (s 1 =0, p 1 =0.01, d 1 =0.01, e 1 =0.004 ± 0.001) T 2 (s 2 =0, p 2 =0.02, d 2 =0.02, e 2 =0.005 ± 0.001) T 3 (s 3 =0, p 3 =0.03, d 3 =0.03, e 3 =0.005 ± 0.002) Figure 8 and Figure 9 are the scheduling of the network and output of the system on the assumption of execution times under uncertainty, ∏(G≤1)=1 and 0≤N(G≤1)≤1. Assume the execution times also subject to triangular distribution, execution times' distribution function of three tasks are shown in Figure 10. It is found that the scheduling is out of order at time 3s and the system is instable when the execution time is under uncertainty. The scheduling is well and the system is stable using the calculated precise time.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: Classical algorithms assume that the execution time of each task keeps constant. It is impossible for networked control system. Because the transmission of data is nonpreemptive on network, it is very important to decide the priorities of tasks and the order of data transmission. The fuzzy execution times affect the decision of priorities seriously. This paper deals with the uncertain time with the fuzzy theory and gets a precise time making each task running orderly. It is proved that this method can improve the scheduling and the stability.
